problem.title: The problem we are solving
problem.statement: Statistical officials must keep learning: survey methods, cloud, GIS, AI, cybersecurity. The training catalogue is vast, yet no one tells an official which courses fit their role, their current skills and what the job needs next. Trainers write assessments by hand. Administrators cannot see capability across the workforce.
lines: Officials: unclear which course to take next.
Trainers: assessments built slowly, by hand.
Administrators: no workforce-level view of skills.

acronym.title: Seven ideas, one name.
acronym.sub: SAMARTH means "capable". Each letter is a promise the platform is built around.

s.text: Know where you stand, backed by evidence, not guesswork.

a1.text: Practice that adjusts to you and an AI tutor that explains.

m.text: Every role has a clear, shared definition of "good".

a2.text: See gaps and trends, with the reason shown.

r.text: The right course, and why it was picked.

t.text: An ordered path, not a pile of courses.

h.text: Statistics, technology, digital governance and leadership together.

how.title: From profile to progress in four steps.

profile.title: Build your profile
profile.body: Share your designation, role, qualifications, experience and past training. SAMARTH AI estimates a starting level for each competency.

gaps.title: See your gaps
gaps.body: Your levels are compared with what your role requires. Gaps are ranked by size and importance, with the reason shown.

path.title: Follow your path
path.body: Get an ordered path from iGOT Karmayogi and NSSTA TPAC programmes (simulated in this prototype), each with why it was recommended.

evidence.title: Prove and update
evidence.body: Quizzes and completed courses add evidence. Levels and recommendations refresh automatically.

visual.why: Why: closes your data privacy gap

tour.title: A look inside the prototype
tour.sub: Every screen below shows demo data.

assessment.headline: Turn any training material into a quiz.
assessment.sub: Upload a PDF, Word, PowerPoint or text file. SAMARTH AI drafts multiple-choice questions, each with an explanation and the passage it came from.
bullets: Grounded in your document, with the source quote shown and checked.
Trainers review, edit and approve before anything reaches learners.
Instant scoring with explanations and personalised feedback.
assessment.note: Video is supported through transcripts. Adaptive difficulty is planned.

mapping.headline: A competency framework built for official statistics.
mapping.sub: Four domains, 43 competencies and six proficiency levels give every role a clear definition of "good".
bullets: Statistical, technical, digital governance and behavioural skills in one view.
Gaps ranked by size, role importance and department priorities.
Every number explained: you can see why a gap matters.
mapping.note: Role requirements are proposed defaults, to be validated with domain experts.

recs.headline: Recommendations that explain themselves.
recs.sub: Each suggested course or programme shows the gap it closes and the level you can expect to reach.
bullets: Two sources: iGOT Karmayogi courses and NSSTA TPAC programmes.
Completed items are excluded and your learning history is considered.
One click opens the course in iGOT (link-out).
recs.note: In this prototype the iGOT Karmayogi and NSSTA data are simulated with sample content. The integration is built behind an adapter so it can connect to the real services once access is granted.

dashboards.headline: The right view for every role.
dashboards.sub: Learners see their radar, gaps and path. Administrators see departments, trends and training effectiveness.
bullets: Learner: competency radar, ranked gaps, learning hours.
Administrator: department-by-domain heatmap, completion and top gaps.
Planned: training effectiveness and an explainable skill-demand forecast (demo uses labelled synthetic history).

language.headline: English and हिन्दी.
language.sub: Switch the whole interface between English and Hindi at any time.
bullets: Hindi interface with a proper Devanagari typeface.
Quiz and feedback translation by AI with trainer review (planned).
Technical terms stay recognisable, for example "stratified sampling" kept in English in brackets.

trust.title: Security and privacy by design.
trust.sub: This is a prototype, so these are design commitments we build and test against, not certifications.

items.tokens: Access tokens live only in secure, HttpOnly cookies, never in browser storage.
items.rbac: Role-based access on every route; people see only what their role allows.
items.sessions: Rotating refresh tokens with reuse detection, account lockout and session control.
items.audit: A hash-chained audit log you can verify for tampering.
items.ai: No names, emails or employee IDs are sent to the AI model.
items.anchor: Optional anchoring of hashes, never personal data, on a public test blockchain.
items.dpdp: Built to align with the principles of India's DPDP Act 2023. We do not claim certification.

standards.label: Standards and frameworks this prototype is designed around. Not certifications or endorsements.
chips: UN Fundamental Principles of Official Statistics

items.q: Is SAMARTH AI an official government website?
items.a: No. It is a student prototype for problem statement SIH26101 (MoSPI). It is not endorsed by or affiliated with MoSPI, NSSTA, iGOT Karmayogi or the Government of India.

items.q: Is it connected to the real iGOT Karmayogi?
items.a: Not yet. The prototype uses a simulated catalogue. Real access needs government credentials. The integration sits behind one adapter so it can be switched when access exists.

items.q: Where do the NSSTA TPAC programmes come from?
items.a: They are sample entries marked illustrative until verified against official sources.

items.q: Can I trust the AI-generated quiz questions?
items.a: Each question must cite a quoted passage from your document, which is checked automatically, and a trainer approves it before learners see it. Reviewing is still a human job.

items.q: Does my personal data go to an AI model?
items.a: By design, no. Names, emails and IDs are removed; only opaque IDs and aggregated competency data are used. See the Privacy Policy for the AI provider and details.
From evidence (quizzes, completions, trainer endorsement, profile, self-declaration) using published formulas. AI suggests; formulas decide; people can override.
The interface works in English and Hindi. AI translation of quizzes and feedback is planned, with trainer review.
The audit log is hash-chained. Optionally, hashes (not personal data) can be anchored on a public test network for demonstration. A permissioned ledger would suit production.
You, and only what each role allows: trainers see their cohorts' results; administrators see their organisation. Access is designed to be role-based and audited.

items.q: Can I use it for real official records?
items.a: No. It is a prototype: use demo or non-sensitive data only.
